quiz.prompt: Your friend is fractal wood-burning with a salvaged microwave transformer, suddenly freezes, and cannot let go of the probe. First move?

options.label: Grab them by the dry cotton hoodie and yank them backward
options.feedback: At 2,000–15,000 V, dry clothing and wooden dowels break down fast—you just volunteered to become Resistor #2 in the same circuit.

options.label: Kick the workbench away with your sneaker
options.feedback: High voltage arcs across damp garage floors and thin rubber soles. Stepping closer before killing power is how double fatalities happen.

options.label: Cut the main breaker or wall power first—then call 911, start CPR, and get an AED
options.feedback: Survived Tuesday! Never touch the victim or bench until power is confirmed dead at the source.

quiz.prompt: A heavy-duty commercial truck tire ran flat for a mile and needs air back up to 105 PSI. Where should you stand?

options.label: Crouched directly facing the sidewall so you can watch the bulge
options.feedback: You just parked your sternum 50 cm from a potential 265 PSI zipper-failure blast cone.

options.label: Inside a steel restraining cage? No—put the TIRE in a steel cage, use a clip-on chuck, and stand ≥2.5 m away along the tread line
options.feedback: Survived Tuesday! And if a commercial tire was driven flat, scrap/inspect it internally before ever re-inflating.

options.label: Lean over the top of the tire holding a short manual gauge
options.feedback: If steel sidewall cords unzip under pressure, the air wave throws nearby bodies across the bay.

quiz.prompt: You pick up 20 lbs of dry ice in a cooler for a road trip in an SUV (no separated trunk). What keeps everyone conscious?

options.label: Tape the cooler lid shut airtight so the CO₂ stays inside
options.feedback: Congratulations—you just built a pressure bomb in your back seat. Dry ice sublimates ~250 L of gas per pound and WILL blow a sealed lid.

options.label: Crack windows wide open, run fresh-air intake (NOT recirculate), and never sleep in the car with dry ice
options.feedback: Survived Tuesday! Heavy CO₂ pools silently from the floor upward with zero odor.

options.label: Turn on cabin A/C recirculation so it stays cool and sublimates slower
options.feedback: Recirculation traps sublimating CO₂ right inside the breathing zone—the exact failure mode in fatal vehicle cases.

clinicalFigures.caption: Three-view left hand radiograph after a high-pressure injection injury showing dark pockets of subcutaneous emphysema dissecting deep along the index finger and palm despite an unimpressive surface pinhole.
clinicalFigures.spoilerNote: Radiograph (X-ray) of pressurized gas/fluid blown inside the hand. Clean skeletal view—no blood.
clinicalFigures.citation: Figure 1 from Fortuna et al. (2022), Journal of Education & Teaching in Emergency Medicine · PMC10332702

clinicalFigures.caption: Forearm radiograph from the same patient proving how far a fingertip high-pressure blast travels—subcutaneous emphysema tracking straight past the wrist into the forearm fascia.
clinicalFigures.spoilerNote: Radiograph (X-ray) showing air/fluid tracking up the forearm.
clinicalFigures.citation: Figure 2 from Fortuna et al. (2022), Journal of Education & Teaching in Emergency Medicine · PMC10332702

quiz.prompt: You accidentally graze your thumb with a 3,000-PSI paint sprayer. It leaves a tiny 2-mm dot that barely bleeds and barely hurts. Next move?

options.label: Wash it with soap, slap a Band-Aid on it, and check it in the morning
options.feedback: The classic amputation trap. High-pressure injection blows solvent deep down tendon sheaths while numb nerves hide the compartment pressure.

options.label: Squeeze the puncture hard to milk the paint back out
options.feedback: Squeezing drives injected fluid deeper along fascial planes and worsens tissue necrosis.

options.label: Go straight to an ER with hand-surgery capability NOW and bring the exact material/SDS label
options.feedback: Survived Tuesday! Early surgical decompression & washout is the difference between keeping a hand and losing it.

clinicalFigures.caption: Axial, sagittal, and 3D-reconstructed thoracic CT revealing a pneumatic nail-gun projectile piercing the anterior sternum directly adjacent to the pericardium and heart (red arrows).
clinicalFigures.spoilerNote: CT scan & 3D ribcage reconstruction—no open surgical gore.
clinicalFigures.citation: Figure 2 from Tombul et al. (2026), Cureus · PMC13163607

quiz.prompt: Three days after a backyard cookout, you develop sharp, localized abdominal pain—but zero fever, normal bowel movements, and a clear plain abdominal X-ray. What crucial sentence must you tell the ER doctor?

options.label: “It’s probably just mild food poisoning, I’ll take Pepto and go home.”
options.feedback: Grill-brush wire perforations are frequently walled off by omentum—normal stool and zero free air do not rule out an abscess.

options.label: “We ate off a grill cleaned with a wire bristle brush—could we check thin-slice CT for a stray bristle?”
options.feedback: Survived Tuesday! Plain X-rays routinely miss thin stainless grill bristles; thin-slice CT catches them.

options.label: “I would have tasted metal if I swallowed a wire.”
options.feedback: Almost no documented wire-bristle ingestion victims ever felt or tasted the wire going down.

clinicalFigures.caption: Actual arterial blood sample drawn in the emergency department displaying classic chocolate-brown methemoglobinemia coloration after over-the-counter 20% benzocaine toothache gel use.
clinicalFigures.spoilerNote: Contains real emergency-department photograph of chocolate-brown blood in a syringe and on gauze. Breakfast optional.
clinicalFigures.citation: Figure 2 from Nappe et al. (2015), Case Reports in Emergency Medicine · PMC4383305

clinicalFigures.caption: The over-the-counter 20% benzocaine oral gel tube brought in by the patient—an ordinary drugstore staple capable of oxidizing Fe²⁺ hemoglobin into non-oxygen-carrying Fe³⁺ methemoglobin.
clinicalFigures.spoilerNote: Product photograph of OTC benzocaine gel tube.
clinicalFigures.citation: Figure 1 from Nappe et al. (2015), Case Reports in Emergency Medicine · PMC4383305

quiz.prompt: After heavy use of OTC benzocaine toothache gel, a patient turns dusky gray and reads SpO₂ 86% despite high-flow oxygen. What test actually proves what is happening?

options.label: Switch to a brand-new finger pulse oximeter on the other hand
options.feedback: Every standard 2-wavelength finger probe hits the exact same ~85% optical plateau in methemoglobinemia.

options.label: Multi-wavelength co-oximetry (which measures MetHb% directly) followed by IV methylene blue
options.feedback: Survived Tuesday! Co-oximetry breaks the 85% lie and IV methylene blue reverses it in ~15 minutes.

options.label: Wait 30 minutes on 100% oxygen to let the lung saturation climb
options.feedback: Dissolved oxygen is already sky-high, but oxidized Fe³⁺ hemoglobin cannot release oxygen to tissues until chemically reduced.

clinicalFigures.caption: Slit-lamp photographs (A–C) and confocal microscopy showing bright double-walled Acanthamoeba cysts invading the cornea (D), alongside cleared cornea after aggressive PHMB 0.08% therapy (E–F).
clinicalFigures.spoilerNote: Close-up ophthalmology slit-lamp eye photography + confocal microscope view.
clinicalFigures.citation: Figure 1 from Pabon et al. (2026), Cureus · PMC13005768

clinicalFigures.caption: Transverse and longitudinal pelvic ultrasound demonstrating significant free intra-abdominal hemorrhage with an empty uterus—in a patient whose urine pregnancy test had just come back negative.
clinicalFigures.citation: Figure 1 from Sheele et al. (2016), Case Reports in Emergency Medicine · PMC5030406

clinicalFigures.spoilerNote: Surgical tray photograph of retrieved marble-sized colorful water beads (no tissue).

clinicalFigures.spoilerNote: Close-up emergency-department photograph of traumatic eye injury with visible blood (hyphema). Click to unseal.

quiz.prompt: A bungee hook snaps back into your eye. The urgent-care pressure check reads normal (16 mmHg) and there is no corneal scratch. Are you cleared?

options.label: Yes—normal eye pressure means no deep structural injury
options.feedback: Pressure, pupil shape, acuity, and internal anatomy answer completely different questions. This patient had 20/800 vision, a torn iris root, and blood inside the eye at 15–17 mmHg.

options.label: No—any blurred vision, irregular pupil, or internal blood demands immediate ophthalmology evaluation regardless of normal pressure
options.feedback: Survived Tuesday! Never rub or press the eye; shield it loosely and get urgent specialist slit-lamp evaluation.

options.label: Put an ice pack firmly over the eyelid and sleep it off
options.feedback: Pressing directly on a traumatized globe can worsen internal bleeding or rupture an occult injury.

clinicalFigures.caption: Brain MRI of a dog with presumptive cycad/sago palm neurotoxicity showing widespread white-matter swelling and cerebellar herniation through the skull base (white arrow)—despite only mildly elevated ALT liver enzymes.
clinicalFigures.citation: Figure 1 from Maeso et al. (2020), Frontiers in Veterinary Science · PMC7456943

clinicalFigures.caption: Follow-up brain MRI after 7 days of aggressive veterinary ICU care: the dramatic white-matter edema and cerebellar displacement completely resolved.
clinicalFigures.spoilerNote: Follow-up grayscale canine brain MRI showing full recovery.
clinicalFigures.citation: Figure 2 from Maeso et al. (2020), Frontiers in Veterinary Science · PMC7456943

quiz.prompt: A relative wearing a prescribed fentanyl pain patch becomes unresponsive in a 106°F hot bath. Paramedics peel the patch off and revive them with Narcan. Why is refusing ER transport still lethal?

options.label: The bathwater soaked through the skin and diluted their sodium
options.feedback: The culprit isn’t water—it’s the huge reservoir of fentanyl that heat already drove deep into the dermis.

options.label: Narcan wears off in 30–90 minutes while the saturated skin depot keeps pumping fentanyl into the bloodstream for up to 17 hours
options.feedback: Survived Tuesday! Peeling the patch stops NEW transfer, not the drug already parked inside the skin.

options.label: Because fentanyl patches explode when removed wet
options.feedback: No explosion—just silent re-narcotization once short-acting naloxone fades.

exam.q: Your buddy touches a homemade fractal wood-burning table and locks up around the probe. Your VERY FIRST move?

options.label: Pull them backward by their dry hoodie
options.why: High voltage punches straight through dry cloth—now paramedics have two cardiac arrests.

options.label: Cut the main breaker or wall power before touching them or the bench
options.why: Correct. Dead circuit first, then 911, CPR, and AED.

options.label: Knock the probe loose with a wooden broom handle
options.why: At 2,000–15,000 V, ordinary wood stops being a reliable insulator.

exam.q: You graze your fingertip with a 3,000-PSI paint sprayer. It leaves a 2-mm pinprick that barely bleeds. What do you do?

options.label: Wash it, bandage it, and see if it swells tomorrow
options.why: Waiting overnight is how tiny pinholes become finger amputations.

options.label: Squeeze hard to push the paint back out
options.why: Squeezing forces solvent deeper along tendon sheaths.

options.label: Go immediately to an ER with hand surgery and bring the paint/solvent label
options.why: Correct. High-pressure injection is an immediate surgical emergency even with minimal pain.

exam.q: A healthy adult uses OTC benzocaine toothache gel, turns gray, and stays stuck at SpO₂ 86% on 100% oxygen. What is lying?

options.label: The standard 2-wavelength finger pulse oximeter—demand co-oximetry and IV methylene blue
options.why: Correct. Methemoglobinemia freezes pulse oximeters near ~85% regardless of real hypoxia.

options.label: The oxygen tank is probably empty
options.why: Arterial dissolved oxygen (PaO₂) is actually sky-high; the iron in hemoglobin is chemically rusted to Fe³⁺.

options.label: The patient is just hyperventilating from anxiety
options.why: Chocolate-brown arterial blood is biochemistry, not anxiety.

exam.q: A patient with a ruptured varicose vein in the ankle is spraying bright blood across the bathroom floor. Fastest life-saving move?

options.label: Wrap a bulky loose towel around the whole calf and sit upright in a chair
options.why: Gravity keeps venous pressure high and bulky towels spread pressure away from the pinpoint leak.

options.label: Lie flat, elevate the leg high above the heart, and press ONE firm finger directly on the pinpoint bleeding hole
options.why: Correct. Elevation drops venous pressure instantly; pinpoint direct pressure seals the leak.

options.label: Soak the foot in cold water to constrict the vein
options.why: Warm or cold soaking hides blood volume loss while exsanguination continues.

exam.q: You drop a single drop of minoxidil hair-growth foam on your pillowcase. Who in the house is in mortal danger?

options.label: Your indoor cat—even trace pillow/hand transfer can trigger fatal feline heart/lung fluid collapse
options.why: Correct. Cats lack the enzymes to clear minoxidil safely; wash hands thoroughly and ban pets from treated pillows.

options.label: Nobody—minoxidil is only risky if someone drinks the bottle
options.why: Documented feline fatalities have occurred from grooming trace residue off owners’ hands and bedding.

options.label: Only houseplants near the bed
options.why: The plants are fine; your cat’s myocardium is not.

exam.q: A toddler swallows a lithium coin (button) battery and is still smiling and breathing normally. Which move is right?

options.label: Wait 24 hours to see if it passes in the diaper
options.why: Button batteries can burn through an esophagus in 2 hours—and keep eroding into the aorta even days later.

options.label: Head straight to the ER for immediate X-ray localization (and if >12 mo old & <12 h since swallow, give honey en route per NBIH guidance)
options.why: Correct. Never wait for symptoms and never induce vomiting.

options.label: Induce vomiting immediately at home
options.why: Vomiting can re-lodge the battery directly against the esophagus or airway.

exam.q: A coworker collapses inside a manure/sludge tank—and the air doesn’t even smell like rotten eggs anymore. Why is that terrifying?

options.label: The gas dissipated, so it’s safe to climb down and pull them out
options.why: That’s how 1 victim becomes 4. High-concentration H₂S paralyzes your sense of smell instantly.

options.label: High-concentration hydrogen sulfide (>100 ppm) knocks out olfactory nerves—NEVER enter without SCBA; call hazmat/911
options.why: Correct. “No smell” in a confined tank can mean lethal knockdown concentration.

options.label: Hold your breath and tie a rope around your waist
options.why: One involuntary gasp at >700 ppm causes instant knockdown collapse.

exam.q: A patient taking prescription nitroglycerin grabs a gas-station “Royal Honey” packet and suddenly feels dizzy with blue-tinted vision. What happened?

options.label: Hidden 60–150 mg sildenafil/tadalafil inside the honey collided with nitroglycerin, triggering distributive blood-pressure shock + retinal PDE6 blue vision
options.why: Correct. Tell paramedics about the supplement immediately so they NEVER give more nitrates.

options.label: Simple raw-honey allergy
options.why: Honey doesn’t inhibit retinal PDE6 or crash blood pressure with nitrates—unlabeled Viagra does.

options.label: Too much natural caffeine
options.why: Caffeine raises blood pressure; PDE5 + nitrate synergy bottoms it out.

exam.q: Your Labrador recovers from backyard wild-mushroom poisoning—her liver ALT dropped 87% by Day 8! On Day 24 she stops eating again, but ALT is nearly normal. What does that mean?

options.label: Her liver is healed, so she’s just being picky
options.why: A falling ALT only means fewer hepatocytes are actively bursting—it never rules out Act Two.

options.label: Treat returning lethargy/anorexia as a fresh ER emergency (this dog crashed into life-threatening Addison’s adrenal crisis with near-normal ALT)
options.why: Correct. The changing patient ALWAYS outranks a pretty lab graph.

options.label: Give extra water and wait a week for the next recheck
options.why: Her blood sugar was 43 mg/dL and potassium was climbing toward cardiac arrest.

exam.q: A healthy homeowner gets struck in the eye by a snapped rusted bungee hook. Eye pressure checks out normal at 16 mmHg. Safe to skip ophthalmology?

options.label: Yes—normal pressure means the eyeball is structurally intact
options.why: This exact patient had 20/800 vision, a torn iris root (iridodialysis), and internal bleeding (hyphema) at 15–17 mmHg.

options.label: No—shield the eye without pressure and get urgent ophthalmology evaluation for any recoil vision drop, irregular pupil, or hyphema
options.why: Correct. Normal pressure never cancels visible internal injury.

options.label: Flush with tap water for 20 minutes and press a cold compress directly onto the eye
options.why: Never press on a blunt-trauma globe—that is for chemical splashes, not mechanical recoil.
